chunks.title: Fire and Explosion Hazard Warnings
chunks.content: Never store or use gasoline/flammable vapors near the dryer; if you smell gas, do not light appliances or use switches/phones, evacuate, and call the gas supplier or fire department from another location.

steps: Do not try to light any appliance
Do not touch any electrical switch or use any phone in the building
Clear the room, building, or area of all occupants
Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow instructions
If you cannot reach the gas supplier, call the fire department

chunks.title: Ductwork Fire Risk
chunks.content: Do not vent the dryer with plastic or thin foil ducting, as flexible venting can collapse, crush, and trap lint, obstructing airflow and increasing fire risk; use only rigid, semi-rigid, or manufacturer-approved flexible metal 4-inch duct.

scenarios.condition: Installing or replacing dryer exhaust duct
steps: Use only rigid, semi-rigid, or approved flexible metal 4-inch diameter duct
Never use plastic or thin foil ducting
Keep duct run as short as possible with minimal elbows
Secure all joints with duct tape, not screws that protrude into the duct

chunks.title: Loading and Operation Warnings
chunks.content: Never dry items contaminated with gasoline, oil, or flammable substances; empty pockets before drying; never reach into a moving drum, and remove clothes promptly after cycle end to avoid fire risk from residual heat reactions.

chunks.title: Steam Function Warnings
chunks.content: Do not open the dryer door during a steam cycle or touch the steam nozzle during/after use; never fill the steam feeder with hot water, gasoline, or other flammable/explosive substances.

chunks.title: Electrical Grounding Requirements
chunks.content: The dryer must be properly grounded via a 3-prong or 4-wire connection per local code; never cut or remove the ground prong, and have a qualified electrician correct any ungrounded outlet.

chunks.title: Booster Fan Prohibition
chunks.content: Do not install a booster fan in the exhaust duct system; follow the dryer manufacturer's installation instructions exactly to avoid fire hazard.

chunks.title: Product Specifications
chunks.content: Covers non-steam (DLE3500*/DLG3501*) and steam (DLEX3700*/DLGX3701*, DLEX3900*/DLGX3901*) dryer models with dimensions 27"W x 30.2"D x 39"H, net weight ~120-127 lb, and IEC drying capacity of 7.4 cu.ft.

rows: NG: 4-10.5 in WC; LP: 8-13 in WC

chunks.title: Installation Clearance Requirements
chunks.content: Recommended clearance is 1 inch on sides/rear (minimum tested), with closet installations requiring upper (48 sq in) and lower (24 sq in) vent openings for heat/moisture buildup prevention.

chunks.title: Level the Dryer
chunks.content: Place a level on top of the dryer and use an adjustable wrench to turn the leveling feet until the dryer sits level front-to-back and side-to-side with all four feet firmly on the floor.

chunks.title: Reverse the Door Swing
chunks.content: Remove decorative screws, latch, and hinge screws while supporting the door weight, flip the door upside down, and reinstall on the opposite side to change swing direction.

chunks.title: Install Side or Bottom Vent Kit
chunks.content: Remove the rear exhaust duct, knock out the desired side/bottom opening, then attach the adapter duct, elbow, and cover plate using the optional side vent kit (part 383EEL9001B).

chunks.title: Stack Dryer on Washer
chunks.content: Attach stacking kit side brackets to the washer top, place the dryer on top fitting its feet into the brackets, then secure the front rail between the units with the included screws.

chunks.title: Connect Steam Model Inlet Hose
chunks.content: Connect the water supply hose to a cold water tap (using a Y-connector if sharing with a washer) and to the dryer's inlet valve, hand-tight plus 2/3 turn, then check for leaks.

chunks.title: Connect Gas Supply
chunks.content: A qualified technician connects the dryer to the gas line using a new stainless steel flexible connector, purges air until gas odor is detected, then checks all connections for leaks with noncorrosive leak-detection fluid.

chunks.title: Wire Electric Dryer Terminal Block
chunks.content: Connect 3-wire or 4-wire power cords/direct wiring to the terminal block per local code, attaching hot leads to outer screws, neutral to center screw, and ground appropriately (4-wire required for new construction after 1996).

chunks.title: Run a Normal Drying Cycle
chunks.content: Clean the lint filter, load laundry, press Power, turn the cycle selector knob to choose a cycle, then press Start/Pause to begin; retrieve clothes promptly when the end chime sounds.

chunks.title: Sort Laundry by Fabric Care Label
chunks.content: Match fabric care label symbols (tumble dry normal/gentle/permanent press/do-not-tumble, and heat level high/medium/low/no-heat) to the appropriate dryer cycle and temperature setting.

chunks.title: Control Panel Overview
chunks.content: The control panel includes the Power button, cycle selector knob, Start/Pause, cycle modifier buttons (Dry Level, Temp., Time Dry, Signal), More/Less Time, cycle option buttons, and (steam models) dedicated steam buttons.

chunks.title: Cycle Guide by Model
chunks.content: Sensor Dry cycles (Normal, Heavy Duty, Bedding, Towels, Antibacterial, etc.) auto-adjust dryness/temperature; Manual Dry cycles (Speed Dry, Air Dry) let users set exact time and temperature.

chunks.title: Use Cycle Modifier and Option Buttons
chunks.content: Use Dry Level, Temp., Time Dry, and Signal buttons to adjust cycle settings; use option buttons like Wrinkle Care, Damp Dry Signal, and Energy Saver to customize drying results.

chunks.title: Use Rack Dry Function
chunks.content: Slide the drying rack into the drum, seat it evenly, place items like sneakers or sweaters flat on it, close the door, select Rack Dry, then choose a temperature (defaults to no heat).

chunks.title: Activate Control Lock and Custom Program
chunks.content: Press and hold Wrinkle Care for 3 seconds to lock/unlock controls; save a frequently-used settings combination by holding Custom PGM for 3 seconds, then recall it anytime with a single press.

chunks.title: Use Steam Fresh and Steam Sanitary Cycles
chunks.content: Select Steam Fresh™ to reduce wrinkles/odors (adjust load size 3/5/big with More/Less Time) or Steam Sanitary™ to sanitize non-washables using cotton/polyester only, not urethane foam or delicates.

rows: Single item or 3 lbs children's clothing

chunks.title: Set Up LG SmartThinQ App and Remote Start
chunks.content: Connect the dryer to a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network, install the SmartThinQ app, then enable Remote Start by holding the Remote Start button 3 seconds before starting a cycle from the phone.

chunks.title: Run Smart Diagnosis via Phone
chunks.content: Call the LG Customer Information Center, hold the phone near the Smart Diagnosis icon, then press and hold Temp. for 3 seconds to transmit diagnostic tones for analysis.

chunks.title: Run Installation Duct Check Test
chunks.content: Remove the rack, close the door, press and hold Signal and Temp. then press Power to activate the test, press Start/Pause, and monitor the Flow Sense LED and display for duct restriction results.

rows: Turn off dryer and call for service
Turn off dryer and call for service
Check power supply/connection or reset breaker/fuse
Confirm gas shutoff valves fully open

chunks.title: Clean the Lint Filter
chunks.content: Pull the lint filter straight up, roll off lint with fingers or vacuum it, and periodically wash with warm soapy water if clogged with fabric softener residue, drying thoroughly before reinstalling.

chunks.title: Clean Dryer Exterior and Interior Surfaces
chunks.content: Clean the exterior with warm water and mild nonabrasive detergent, wipe the door opening/seal and window with a damp soft cloth, and clean the stainless drum with a stainless-specific cleaner.

chunks.title: Clean Around and Under Dryer and Maintain Ductwork
chunks.content: Vacuum lint and dust from around and under the dryer regularly, and check vent ductwork monthly for lint buildup, cleaning it at least annually or immediately if airflow/drying performance drops.

chunks.title: Dryer Won't Start or Won't Heat
chunks.content: Covers causes like unplugged cord, blown fuse/tripped breaker, gas supply off, or Energy Saver option masking heat at cycle start.

rows: Power cord not plugged in properly
Ensure plug is securely in grounded outlet
Reset breaker or replace fuse; do not increase capacity
Reset breaker/fuse; electric dryers can run without heat on partial circuit failure
Confirm house and dryer gas shutoff valves are open
Deselect Energy Saver for immediate heat at cycle start

chunks.title: Clothes Take Too Long to Dry
chunks.content: Common causes include blocked/dirty/long exhaust ducts, improperly sorted loads, dirty lint filter, overloading/underloading, or Energy Saver mode.

rows: Clothes take too long to dry
Check ducts for obstructions; ensure dampers open freely

Clothes take too long to dry
Divide large loads; add extra items to very small loads
Expect variation based on fabric type, load size, washer spin quality

chunks.title: Fabric Quality Issues (Static, Lint, Wrinkles, Shrinking)
chunks.content: Addresses greasy spots, wrinkling, shrinking, lint transfer, and static buildup, generally caused by improper sorting, overdrying, or fabric softener misuse.

rows: Fabric softener misuse or mixed dirty/clean loads
Follow softener instructions; dry only clean items
Overdrying or left in dryer too long
Use shorter time/Less Dry setting; use Wrinkle Care option
Use low or no-heat setting per fabric label
Filter not cleaned; laundry not sorted
Clean filter; separate lint producers from lint trappers
Use fabric softener or Reduce Static option; shorten dry time

chunks.title: Wi-Fi Connection Issues
chunks.content: Covers wrong SSID/password, mobile data left on, non-2.4GHz router, and excessive distance from router as common causes of failed SmartThinQ pairing.

rows: Turn off mobile data before registering
Move router closer or add a Wi-Fi repeater

chunks.title: Steam Function Issues
chunks.content: Covers normal behaviors (water dripping, condensation, invisible steam, drum pausing) versus real problems like water level error requiring service.

rows: Water drips from nozzle at cycle start
Garments still wrinkled after Steam Fresh
Steam does not generate, no error code
Unplug dryer and call for service
Drum does not turn during steam cycle

chunks.title: Duct Blockage Error Codes (Flow Sense)
chunks.content: Error codes d75/d80/d90/d95 indicate 75-95% duct blockage; stop using the dryer until the exhaust system is cleaned/repaired since severe restriction is a fire and property-damage risk.

rows: Turn off dryer and call for service
Check power cord connection to terminal block
Stop use; clean/repair exhaust before continuing
Check Filter indicator on during cycle
Clean lint filter; pause cycle to clean if needed for high-lint loads

chunks.title: Special Electrical Requirements for Mobile/Manufactured Homes
chunks.content: Mobile/manufactured home installs require a 4-wire electrical connection, permanent floor attachment for gas dryers, outdoor venting (never under the home), and a minimum 25 sq in fresh-air opening.

tasks.title: Clean the Lint Filter
tasks.description: Remove and clean lint from the filter before or after every drying load.
tasks.justification: A clogged lint filter reduces airflow, increases drying time, wastes energy, and raises fire risk.
tasks.instructions_text: Pull the lint filter straight up out of the drum opening and roll the lint off with your fingers or vacuum it clean. Push the filter firmly back into place until it clicks. If it looks dirty or clogged from fabric softener residue, wash it in warm soapy water and let it dry completely before reinstalling.

tasks.title: Clean and Inspect Exhaust Ductwork
tasks.description: Check the vent ductwork for lint buildup monthly and have it professionally cleaned at least once a year.
tasks.justification: Blocked or dirty ducts restrict airflow, greatly extend drying time, waste energy, and create a serious fire hazard.
tasks.instructions_text: Inspect the outside vent hood and full duct run for lint buildup, damage, or crushing at least once a month. Have the ductwork professionally cleaned at least once a year, or immediately if you notice reduced airflow or longer drying times.

tasks.title: Vacuum Around and Under the Dryer
tasks.description: Vacuum lint and dust that accumulates around and underneath the dryer.
tasks.justification: Prevents lint and dust accumulation near the appliance, which is a fire and cleanliness concern.
tasks.instructions_text: Move the dryer if possible and vacuum up lint and dust from the floor around and underneath it. Do this regularly, especially if you notice buildup near the exhaust opening.

tasks.title: Clean the Dryer Exterior
tasks.description: Wipe down the outside cabinet of the dryer with mild detergent and water.
tasks.justification: Cosmetic only — keeps the exterior finish clean and free of spills and stains.
tasks.instructions_text: Wipe the outside of the dryer with warm water and a mild, nonabrasive household detergent. Immediately wipe off any spills with a soft, damp cloth.

tasks.title: Clean the Door Seal, Window, and Drum Interior
tasks.description: Wipe the door opening, seal, and window, and clean the stainless steel drum with an appropriate cleaner.
tasks.justification: Prevents lint and dust buildup around the door seal and keeps the drum interior clean; skipping affects appearance and can damage the door seal over time.
tasks.instructions_text: Wipe around the door opening and seal with a soft, damp cloth to prevent lint and dust buildup. Clean the window with a soft cloth dampened with warm water and mild detergent, then wipe dry. Clean the stainless steel drum with a conventional stainless steel cleaner following the manufacturer's instructions.

tasks.title: Level the Dryer
tasks.description: Verify and adjust the leveling feet so the dryer sits flat and stable during installation.
tasks.justification: An unlevel dryer can vibrate, walk, cause noise, and clothes may not tumble or dry properly.
tasks.instructions_text: Place a level across the top of the dryer and gently push on the top corners to check for rocking. Use an adjustable wrench to turn the leveling feet, raising or lowering each corner, until the dryer is level front-to-back and side-to-side with all four feet firmly on the floor.

re_check_triggers.description: Dryer vibrates excessively, walks, or makes noise during operation

tasks.title: Verify Proper Electrical Grounding
tasks.description: Confirm the dryer is connected to a properly grounded outlet or wiring system per local code.
tasks.justification: Improper grounding creates a serious risk of electric shock or fire.
tasks.instructions_text: Have a qualified electrician verify the wall outlet or wiring is properly grounded according to local codes before connecting the dryer. Do not modify, cut, or remove the grounding prong from the power cord.

re_check_triggers.description: You notice shocks, sparks, or burning smells near the dryer or outlet

tasks.title: Connect and Test Gas Supply Line
tasks.description: Have a qualified technician connect the dryer to the gas supply and check all connections for leaks.
tasks.justification: A gas leak or improper connection is a fire and explosion hazard.
tasks.instructions_text: A qualified installer or gas supplier connects the dryer to the gas line using a new stainless steel flexible connector, purges air from the line, and checks all connections with a noncorrosive leak-detection fluid — never an open flame.

re_check_triggers.description: You smell gas near the dryer or connections

tasks.title: Verify Exhaust Duct Installation and Routing
tasks.description: Confirm the exhaust duct is the correct 4-inch metal type, properly routed with minimal elbows, and vented to the outdoors.
tasks.justification: Improper venting causes lint accumulation, extended drying times, and a significant fire hazard, and is not covered under warranty if incorrect.
tasks.instructions_text: Confirm the duct is rigid, semi-rigid, or approved flexible metal, 4 inches in diameter, with the male end of each section facing away from the dryer and joints sealed with duct tape. Route the duct as short and straight as possible using as few elbows as possible, and confirm it vents to the outdoors with a damper-equipped hood.

re_check_triggers.description: Drying times become excessively long or you notice reduced airflow at the vent hood

tasks.title: Run Installation Duct Check Test
tasks.description: Run the built-in installation test after setup to verify the exhaust system has adequate airflow.
tasks.justification: Confirms the exhaust system is not restricted before regular use, preventing long-term fire risk and poor drying performance.
tasks.instructions_text: With the drum empty and door closed, press and hold Signal and Temp., then press Power to activate the test; on glass touch panels press Power first then immediately hold Temp. and Signal. Press Start/Pause to begin the test cycle and check the Flow Sense indicator and display for results when it ends.

re_check_triggers.description: The Flow Sense indicator lights or an error code like d75-d95 appears

tasks.title: Check Duct Condition After Flow Sense Alert
tasks.description: Inspect and clean or repair the exhaust duct whenever the Flow Sense indicator or a d75-d95 error code appears.
tasks.justification: A severely restricted exhaust system is dangerous and could result in a fire or other property damage.
tasks.instructions_text: Stop using the dryer if the Flow Sense LED turns on or a d75, d80, d90, or d95 code appears. Check the outside vent hood and full duct run for lint buildup, blockage, or damage, and clean or repair the exhaust system before continuing to use the dryer.

re_check_triggers.description: Flow Sense indicator remains active for more than five cycles after clearing a restriction

tasks.title: Wash the Lint Filter When Clogged
tasks.description: Wash the lint filter in warm soapy water when it becomes very dirty or clogged with fabric softener residue.
tasks.justification: Fabric softener residue can coat and clog the filter mesh in a way that vacuuming or rolling off lint cannot fix, reducing airflow and drying performance.
tasks.instructions_text: If the lint filter looks clogged or dirty even after removing loose lint, wash it in warm, soapy water. Allow it to dry thoroughly before reinstalling it in the dryer.

weekly.title: Weekly Care
steps: Clean lint from the filter before or after every load
Wipe up any spills on the exterior with a damp cloth
Check the vent hood outside for obvious blockage

deep_clean.title: Deep Clean / Periodic Maintenance
steps: Wash the lint filter in warm soapy water if clogged with fabric softener residue
Wipe the door opening, seal, and window with a soft damp cloth
Clean the stainless steel drum with a stainless steel cleaner
Vacuum lint and dust from around and underneath the dryer
Inspect the vent ductwork monthly and have it professionally cleaned at least annually

warranty.coverage: LG provides parts and labor for one year from original retail purchase to repair or replace defective parts due to material or workmanship defects under normal home use; the dryer drum is covered for parts only for ten years.
exclusions: Service trips to deliver, pick up, install, or instruct on product operation
Failure during power outages or inadequate electrical service
Damage from leaky/broken/frozen water pipes or inadequate water/air supply
Damage from corrosive atmosphere or misuse contrary to owner's manual
Damage from accidents, pests, lightning, wind, fire, floods, or acts of God
Incorrect electrical current/voltage or commercial/industrial use
Transportation and handling damage unless reported within 1 week of delivery
Conversion from natural gas to LP gas or vice versa

confidence.notes: Manual is a comprehensive user manual covering install, operation, and troubleshooting for both gas/electric and steam/non-steam variants; installation steps were classified as setup tasks per guidelines, and professional-only gas/electrical steps were described without DIY instructions.
